overview.text: The Yellow-faced Whip Snake is a thin, fast, venomous snake found across much of Australia.

identification.text: Thin with a narrow yellowish head, a pale ring around each eye and a dark curved mark along the upper lip.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 80 cm on average, up to 1 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Every Australian state except Tasmania, from coastal forest to dry inland scrub.

behaviour.text: Active by day, fast and nervous - it flees quickly when disturbed. It slows down in winter.

diet.text: Mainly small lizards that are active by day, and lizard eggs.

reproduction.text: Lays eggs; many females may use the same nest, and some nests have held 500 to 600 eggs.

funfacts.text: Lots of females can lay their eggs in the same nest - up to hundreds of eggs together.

recognise.text: Pale ring around the eye and dark mark on the lip.
